case_title: MOSIRUDDIN MUNSHI v. MD. SIRAJ AND ANOTHER
neutral_facts: The accused, through a public servant, represented that they could arrange for a plot of land for sale. The accused and the complainant entered into an agreement for sale, and the complainant paid a large sum of money in cash. The accused failed to hand over the title documents, leading the complainant to issue a legal notice. When other methods to compel the accused to complete the sale failed, the complainant filed a criminal complaint against the accused under Sections 420 and 1208 of the IPC. The trial court forwarded the complaint for investigation, treating it as a First Information Report. The accused then filed an application under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings. The High Court quashed the complaint proceedings, declaring it a civil transaction. The case was remitted to the High Court for a fresh decision, which again quashed the proceedings. The complainant appealed to the Supreme Court, which allowed the appeal and set aside the High Court's order.
